page: Microsoft Azure L8as_v3 is a storage-optimized virtual machine from the LASv3 family, running on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor. It features an x86_64 AMD EPYC 7763 processor with 8 dedicated vCPUs, derived from 4 physical cores with 2 threads per core, operating at a clock speed of 3.525 GHz. The CPU configuration includes 32 KB of L1d cache, 0.5 MB of L2 cache, and 32 MB of L3 cache. The system is equipped with 64.0 GB of system memory, providing 8.0 GB of RAM per core, and includes a bundled 2002 GB local NVMe SSD. No dedicated GPU is present on this instance.

In benchmark evaluations, the L8as_v3 demonstrates strong single-core CPU performance, scoring 2710.47 in stress-ng tests, which places it in the top 25% of tested instances. Multi-core CPU performance and memory bandwidth for small, cached blocks fall within the average tier. However, the system exhibits weaker performance in large-block, uncached memory operations, with read bandwidth at 38.93 GB/sec and write bandwidth at 22.95 GB/sec. Database operations, Redis SET operations, and static web serving throughput consistently register in the average range.

The qualitative cost profile of the L8as_v3 is defined by its high local storage density and generous memory-to-vCPU ratio, making it a resource-dense option for workloads requiring fast local scratch space without the overhead of external storage. The primary tradeoff lies in the uncached memory bandwidth limitations and weaker multi-threaded decompression speeds. Given these characteristics, this server is well-suited for database hosting, local caching layers, medium-scale web serving, and data processing tasks that benefit from high-capacity local NVMe storage and balanced memory allocation.
